title: DLMF 4.12 Generalized Logarithms and Exponentials: A generalized exponential function \phi(x) satisfies the equations
summary: DLMF 4.12 Generalized Logarithms and Exponentials: A generalized exponential function \phi(x) satisfies the equations
body: NIST DLMF section 4.12 (Generalized Logarithms and Exponentials) says: "A generalized exponential function \phi(x) satisfies the equations and is strictly increasing when 0\leq x\leq 1 . Its inverse \psi(x) is called a generalized logarithm . It, too, is strictly increasing when 0\leq x\leq 1 , and These functions are not unique. The simplest choice is given by where \ell is the positive integer determined by the condition Both \phi(x) and \psi(x) are continuously differentiable. For further information, see Clenshaw et al. ( 1986 ) . For C^{\infty} generalized logarithms, see Walker ( 1991 ) . For analytic generalized logarithms, see Kneser ( 1950 ) ." Equation 4.12.5 on the page has alt text "\phi(x)=\psi(x)=x,". Equation 4.12.6 on the page has alt text "\phi(x)=\ln\left(x+1\right),". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
